# port-helpers

Header-only C11 helpers shared by the SDL3 ports (ngo, OpenBattleGaiden, OpenIdolExchanger): launcher menus, touch controls, ROM finding and picking, input binding, LAN lockstep play, settings files and a debug overlay.

Everything is plain structs and functions. There are no callbacks: modules hand back results (`struct ph_launch`, `PH_NET_READY`, `PH_TOUCH_EDIT_DONE`, ...) and the game decides what to do.

## Modules

| Header | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `ph_hash.h` | CRC32, FNV-1a 32/64, SHA-1 |
| `ph_zip.h` | Zip central directory, inflate, placing ROM parts by CRC or name (with interleave step) |
| `ph_files.h` | User folder, ROM search (`struct ph_search`), native file picker, drag and drop, imports, save-state slot paths |
| `ph_ios.h` | iOS document picker, haptic tap, view fit (Objective-C, iOS only) |
| `ph_view.h` | Integer/fit/stretch scaling, TV pixel aspect, safe area, points and pixel density, event coordinates |
| `ph_draw.h` | Anti-aliased rounded rects, circles, lines and Inter text (Medium and Bold, kerned), drawn in output pixels, and textures from PNG bytes |
| `ph_inter.h` | Inter outlines and kerning as C data, generated by `tools/inter.py` |
| `ph_settings.h` | Settings tables (choices, numbers, text) and the `key=value` file format |
| `ph_crt.h` | Sharp, nearest, smooth or CRT filtering of the game picture, with scanlines, a phosphor mask, curvature and glow |
| `ph_crt_shader.h` | The CRT shader as SPIR-V and Metal, generated from `shaders/crt.frag` by `tools/crt.py` |
| `ph_input.h` | Keyboard and gamepad bindings for up to 4 players, rebinding by capture, hotplug |
| `ph_touch.h` | On-screen d-pad, stick, buttons and pills with portrait/landscape layouts, haptics and a drag-to-arrange editor |
| `ph_menu.h` | Immediate-mode menu model with keyboard, gamepad, mouse and touch navigation, and a themeable renderer in the OpenBattleGaiden style |
| `ph_net.h` | UDP LAN discovery and two-player input-delay lockstep with resends and desync checks |
| `ph_debug.h` | Tabbed debug overlay: text, buttons, toggles, steppers, plots, hex memory view, performance and network panels |
| `ph_config.h` | One settings file for the game's settings, bindings, touch layout and LAN name (`ph_config_load`, `ph_config_save`) |
| `ph_launcher.h` | The full launcher built from the pieces above: main, pause, settings, mappings, ROM, LAN, save and load pages |
| `ph_script.h` | UI scripts for automated runs: keys, held keys, text, clicks, taps, drops, window sizes and screenshots on given frames |
| `ph.h` | Includes all of the above and defines `PH_VERSION` |

## Adding it to a port

Compile the implementation into exactly one C file:

```c
#define PH_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "ph.h"
```

Every other file just includes the headers it needs. The headers are safe to include from C++ (for example ImGui code), but the implementation file must be C.

With CMake, `add_subdirectory(port-helpers)` and link `port_helpers`. It brings in SDL3 and the extra platform libraries listed below. On iOS it also adds `ph_ios.m` and turns on `-fobjc-arc` (C files ignore it), so the port only needs `enable_language(OBJC)`. Without CMake, compile `ph_ios.m` with `-fobjc-arc` yourself; it refuses to build without it.

Each port keeps its own copy of this folder. `tools/sync.sh ../game/third_party/port-helpers` replaces a copy with this one, and `tools/sync.sh --check` lists what differs. `PH_VERSION` goes up when the API changes.

`ph_embed(target name file)` turns a file into a static library holding `const unsigned char name[]` and `const size_t name_size`, so a launcher picture ships inside the game on every platform. Without CMake, run `cmake -DINPUT=file -DOUTPUT=file.c -DNAME=name -P tools/embed.cmake` and compile the output.

| Platform | Link | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All | SDL3 | |
| Windows | `ws2_32`, `iphlpapi` | MSVC picks these up from `#pragma comment` |
| iOS | UIKit, UniformTypeIdentifiers | Info.plist needs `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`. Finding and hosting games on the LAN page needs the `com.apple.developer.networking.multicast` entitlement; `ph_net_join` with an address works without it. Set `UIFileSharingEnabled` and `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace` so players can drop ROMs into Documents. |
| Android | | Needs the `INTERNET` permission. Some devices drop broadcasts unless the app holds a Wi-Fi multicast lock (`CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE`). |
| Linux | | `ph.h` defines `_DEFAULT_SOURCE` when it is the first include of the implementation file. |

## The main loop

```c
while (SDL_PollEvent(&event)) {
    if (ph_debug_event(&debug, renderer, &event)) {
        continue;
    }
    act(ph_launcher_event(&launcher, renderer, &event));
}
act(ph_launcher_update(&launcher));
```

Pass every event to the launcher, open or closed. While the game runs, it hands events to `input` and `touch` and watches for a pause.

`act` is a `switch` on `launch.kind`:

- `PH_LAUNCH_PAUSE` means the launcher just opened the pause menu over the game. Clear your audio stream here.
- `PH_LAUNCH_PLAY`, `RESUME`, `RESET`, `END` and `QUIT` drive the game. `END` comes from Quit to launcher, Leave LAN game, and a LAN game that was lost. The launcher has already stopped LAN play and opened the main page.
- `SAVE_STATE` and `LOAD_STATE` carry the slot number in `value`.
- `SETTING` gives the index of the setting that changed. `PH_SETTINGS_ALL` means defaults were restored.
- `SAVE_CONFIG` means persist now.
- `ROM_PICKED` leaves the path in `launcher.picked`. It never arrives during a game: the launcher refuses the file with "Quit to the launcher to change the ROM."
- `ROM_RESCAN` asks you to look for the ROM again. It comes after Remove imported ROM (the launcher deletes `rom_import` itself) and when an iOS or Android app comes back to the front.
- `NETPLAY` means a LAN session is connected and the game should start. `value` is the local player.
- `CUSTOM` returns the id of one of your `launcher.items`.

The game owns the decisions: call `ph_launcher_close` when play starts. While the launcher is open, give it the screen with `ph_launcher_draw`.

While the game runs (the launcher is closed), the launcher pauses by itself, as OpenBattleGaiden does:

- **Escape, Android Back, or a gamepad's Select or Guide button:** opens the pause menu.
- **The window losing focus:** opens the pause menu, except during LAN play.
- **A tap on a `PH_TOUCH_PAUSE` control:** opens the pause menu.

The pause menu uses the same card as the main page, with no title, drawn over the shaded game frame, so draw the game first and the launcher after it. Resume, Save state and Load state (when `slots` is set), Reset and your `items` for `PH_PAGE_PAUSE` are at the top. Settings and Quit to launcher are at the bottom. In LAN play Quit to launcher becomes Leave LAN game, and the save, load and reset items are left out.

`ph_launcher_close` blocks any button still held from the menu until it is released (`ph_input_block_held`), and drops the fingers that were on the screen. So the button that picked Resume doesn't also jump.

The launcher is configured by filling in plain fields after `ph_launcher_init(launcher, window)`: `settings`, `sections`, `input`, `touch`, `net`, `items`, `slots`, `rom_hint`, `rom_description`, `rom_patterns`, `rom_import`. Leave a pointer `NULL` to drop that page.

- **Settings pages:** two-level nested settings. `PH_PAGE_SETTINGS` lists each populated setting category (`Display`, `Sound`, `Game`, etc.), `Controls` (`Mappings`, touch options, and `Arrange touch controls`), and `System` (custom settings actions, `ROM`, and `Restore defaults`, which also resets the touch options). Selecting a category pushes its settings card on top of the stack.
- **LAN page:** Host, then the games found on the network. Host opens the Hosting page, where the player can change the name the other device sees.
- **ROM state:** `ph_launcher_rom_found(launcher, path)` marks the ROM ready and names it. `ph_launcher_rom_failed(launcher, path, problem)` says what is wrong, and the main page shows it in red. `ph_launcher_rom_clear` forgets it. A ROM found in the user folder can be removed from the ROM page when `rom_import` names it.
- **ROM page during a game:** it shows "Quit to the launcher to change the ROM." instead of Choose file and Remove.

Games that draw their own launcher with ROM fonts can use `ph_menu` directly. Build rows each frame with `ph_menu_begin(menu, title, style)`/`ph_menu_add`/`ph_menu_end`, feed events to `ph_menu_event`, and draw each row yourself at `ph_menu_row_rect`.

## Look

Everything is laid out on a crisp virtual canvas scaled to fit the safe area (`16:9` widescreen, `4:3` `240p`/`480p` CRTs, and portrait). Root menu cards (`Main`, `Pause`) always anchor in the **top-left**; pushed submenus cascade **on top and slightly down-right**, keeping parent cards visible underneath with breadcrumb highlights and a subtle receding veil. Missing-ROM hints appear in a dedicated box in the **bottom-right**, and `launcher.menu.logo` is drawn in the **top-right**.

| Style | Used for | Layout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PH_STYLE_LIST` | Category settings, Mappings, LAN, Hosting, save slots | Title, rows, `< value >` steppers / bars and a scrollbar |
| `PH_STYLE_BIG` | Main, pause, Settings categories, ROM | Snug action cards (`Play`, `Settings`, category pickers, etc.). Root main and pause cards have no title. |

- **Note tones:** set `row->tone` on notes. `PH_TONE_DIM`, `STRONG` (bold accent), `WARNING` and `ERROR`.
- **Back button:** any page pushed on top of another gets a back arrow beside its title. Escape, Android Back and the gamepad's East button do the same. There are no Back rows.
- **Selection:** the selected row is drawn in the accent colour, list rows on a soft rounded highlight. There is no selection bar.
- **Touch mode:** turns on after a finger touch, or from the start on phones. It makes rows taller and text bigger, and shows no selection, only the row under a finger while it is pressed.
- **Notices:** appear in a dark pill near the bottom.
- **Prompts:** `ph_menu_prompt` draws the modal used while rebinding a button.

Colours come from `struct ph_menu_theme`: `background`, `shade` (over the game when paused), `panel`, `text`, `bright`, `dim`, `accent`, `heading`, `warning` and `error`. The default theme is neutral grey with a black card and OBG's pumpkin accent. Set `launcher.menu.theme` (and optionally `debug.theme`) to your own `struct ph_menu_theme`, or build one in one call with `ph_theme_make(tile_a, tile_b, panel, border, accent)`.

- **`launcher.menu.background`:** a texture that covers the whole screen behind launcher pages, cropped to fill. `ph_texture_png(renderer, data, size)` makes one from embedded PNG bytes.
- **`launcher.menu.logo`:** shown on the main page in place of a title. There is no title text, so set it once the ROM is loaded (games can draw it from ROM graphics) and clear it when the ROM goes away.

Neither is drawn over the game in the pause menu. `tests/test.c` has OBG's green palette as `green_theme`.

## Text

```c
ph_text(renderer, "Paused", x, y, 36, PH_TEXT_BOLD, ph_color(0xFFFFFF, 1));
float width = ph_text_width("Paused", 36, PH_TEXT_BOLD);
```

- **Size and position:** `size` is the line height in pixels, and `y` is the top of the line. Inter's capitals sit in the middle of that box, so `ph_text_centered` centres text on a point.
- **Characters:** printable ASCII, `·` and `…`. Anything else draws as `?`. `ph_text_fit` shortens text with `…`.
- **Rendering:** glyphs are rasterized at the exact pixel size into a cached atlas per renderer, size and weight.
- **Regenerating the font:** `pip install fonttools`, then `python tools/inter.py > ph_inter.h`.

Inter is © The Inter Project Authors, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. `ph_inter.h` is derived from it, so ship `fonts/LICENSE-Inter.txt`, or its text in your credits, with your game.

## Settings files

Each module reads and writes its own keys, so one file in the user folder holds everything:

```c
struct ph_config config = { settings, count, &input, &touch, &net };
ph_config_load(&config, "settings.txt");
ph_config_save(&config, "settings.txt");
```

`ph_config_load` resets the settings to their defaults first and returns 0 when there is no file yet. Leave `input`, `touch` or `net` `NULL` to skip them. `ph_config_take(config, key, value)` takes one pair, for ports that read keys of their own with `ph_next_pair`.

A setting is a choice if `choices` is set, text if `text` is set, and a number otherwise (`minimum`, `maximum`, `step`, `unit`, `zero` label).

## Finding the ROM

```c
const char *const names[] = { "wjammers.zip", "wjammers.neo" };
struct ph_search search = { names, 2, explicit_paths, explicit_count, 0 };
char path[PH_PATH_SIZE];
while (ph_search_next(&search, path, sizeof path)) {
    if (try_load(path)) {
        break;
    }
}
```

Explicit paths are checked first, then each name in the user folder, Documents, the app folder and the working directory. A picked or dropped file arrives as `PH_LAUNCH_ROM_PICKED`. Keep a copy with `ph_import(data, size, launcher.rom_import)` so the next launch finds it in the user folder, search again, then call `ph_launcher_rom_imported`. It opens the main page when the ROM is ready and shows "ROM loaded." or the problem. `ph_file_name(path)` gives the part after the last slash. `ph_zip_place` loads multi-part sets by CRC, or by name when `crc` is 0, with a `step` for interleaved chips.

## LAN play

Every machine runs the same deterministic game and exchanges only inputs.

```c
uint32_t inputs[2];
switch (ph_net_frame(&net, local_inputs, inputs)) {
case PH_NET_READY:
    run_one_frame(inputs[0], inputs[1]);
    if (ph_net_check_due(&net)) {
        ph_net_check(&net, hash_of_game_state());
    }
    break;
case PH_NET_WAIT:
    break;
case PH_NET_LOST:
    show(net.message);
    break;
}
```

`ph_net_frame` never blocks. Call it again next loop while it says `PH_NET_WAIT`, or sleep briefly with `ph_net_wait`.

- **Starting:** on `PH_LAUNCH_NETPLAY`, call `ph_net_begin(&net)`. It stops looking for games and marks the session as playing (`ph_net_playing`).
- **Stalls:** `ph_net_stalled` is true once the other side has been silent for a quarter of a second. The launcher then shows "Waiting for the other player..." by itself.
- **Losing the game:** when a playing session fails (the other player left, went quiet, or went out of sync), the next `ph_launcher_update` stops LAN play, opens the main page with the reason and returns `PH_LAUNCH_END`.
- **Identity:** `identity` in `ph_net_init` should hash the build version and the ROM, so mismatched games are refused with a clear message.
- **Rules:** set the `rules` bytes for match options. `ph_net_agreed_rules(&net)` returns the host's rules on both machines.
- **Discovery:** the host listens on `port` for discovery and plays on the first free port after it.
- **Input delay:** chosen from measured round-trip time unless a player picks one.
- **Desync checks:** state hashes are compared every `check_interval` frames (default 60). A mismatch ends the session with "The two games went out of sync at frame N."

## Touch controls

Each control is placed as a fraction of the safe area (`x`, `y`) and sized in points (`width`, `height`; height 0 makes it round).

- **Reading input:** give each control the action bits it presses in `actions`, then OR `ph_touch_mask(&touch, &input)` into player 1's `ph_input_mask`. The pad and stick press whichever actions player 1's gamepad d-pad is bound to. `touch.held` (a bit per control), `touch.directions` (`PH_TOUCH_UP|DOWN|LEFT|RIGHT`) and `ph_touch_tapped` (for controls with `tap` set) are there for anything else.
- **Pausing:** a `PH_TOUCH_PAUSE` control is a round button with a pause icon. The launcher opens the pause menu when it is tapped.
- **When it shows:** the overlay appears after a finger touches the screen, and hides when a key, gamepad or mouse is used. `mode` can force it on or off.
- **Arranging:** players drag controls around from Settings › Controls › Arrange touch controls. Positions are saved per orientation.

## Window

- **Size:** `ph_view_window_size(window, width, height, pixel_aspect, scale)` sizes the window to a whole multiple of the game screen, shrinks the multiple until it fits the display, and centres it.
- **Fullscreen key:** `ph_view_fullscreen_key(event)` is true for F11, Alt+Enter and Cmd+Enter on desktop. Check it before passing the event to the launcher.

## Picture

`ph_crt` draws the game picture with one of four filters: Sharp (smooth edges between big pixels), Nearest, Smooth, or CRT. The CRT filter follows Timothy Lottes' public domain CRT shader. Each line of the picture is a beam with a dark gap below it, and bright lines widen as in crt-guest-advanced. On top of that come a phosphor mask in window pixels, glow, and a curved screen with rounded corners.

```c
renderer = ph_crt_create_renderer(window);
ph_crt_settings(&crt, &settings[SETTING_CRT], SECTION_DISPLAY);
ph_config_load(&config, "settings.txt");
ph_crt_open(&crt, renderer);
ph_crt_settings(&crt, &settings[SETTING_CRT], SECTION_DISPLAY);

ph_crt_draw(&crt, picture, ph_view_fit(ph_view_safe(renderer), 320, 224, 1, scaling));
```

- **Renderer:** the shader needs SDL's GPU renderer, which `ph_crt_create_renderer` asks for. If that can't start, it returns SDL's default renderer. Then the CRT filter draws like Nearest, Scanlines draws plain dark lines over the picture, and the mask, curve and glow rows stay hidden. On Windows the shader needs Vulkan.
- **Settings:** `ph_crt_settings` fills `PH_CRT_SETTINGS` rows of the settings table: Filter, Scanlines, CRT mask, CRT curve and CRT glow. The values live in `struct ph_crt`. Leave room for them (`SETTING_VOLUME = SETTING_CRT + PH_CRT_SETTINGS`), and fill them before `ph_settings_reset` or `ph_config_load`. Call it again after `ph_crt_open` and after each setting change, since the mask, curve and glow rows only show while the CRT filter is chosen and the shader is running.
- **Drawing:** the picture is any texture. `ph_crt_draw` sets its scale mode and reads its size. The CRT looks best at integer scaling and 3x or more.
- **Changing the shader:** edit `shaders/crt.frag`, install `glslang` and `spirv-cross`, and run `python3 tools/crt.py > ph_crt_shader.h`. Ports build with the generated header, so they need no shader tools.

## UI scripts

`ph_script_load(&script, path)` reads lines of `<frame> <command> <argument>`, and `ph_script_step(&script, window, renderer)` runs the ones that are due, once per presented frame.

| Command | Argument | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | SDL key name | Presses and releases a key |
| `down`, `up` | SDL key name | Holds a key down, then lets it go |
| `text` | text | Types text into a focused text field |
| `click`, `tap` | x y | Clicks the mouse or taps a finger at window coordinates |
| `drop` | path | Drops a file on the window |
| `size` | width height | Resizes the window |
| `shot` | path | Saves the screen, as PNG when the path ends in `.png`, BMP otherwise |
| `quit` | | Sends a quit event |

## Wiring a port

1. **Start up:** call `ph_files_init(organization, application)`, then `ph_input_init` with `ph_input_defaults`, `ph_touch_init` and `ph_net_init`, fill the picture rows with `ph_crt_settings`, then `ph_config_load`. None of these need a window.
2. **Window:** create it, make the renderer with `ph_crt_create_renderer`, size the window with `ph_view_window_size`, and call `ph_crt_open`. Draw each game frame with `ph_crt_draw`.
3. **Launcher:** call `ph_launcher_init`, fill in its fields, look for the ROM, and report it with `ph_launcher_rom_found` or `ph_launcher_rom_failed`. Open `PH_PAGE_MAIN`, or start the game at once when the player asked for that on the command line.
4. **Events:** pass every event to `ph_launcher_event`. Check `ph_view_fullscreen_key` and the debug overlay first.
5. **Every loop:** `act(ph_launcher_update(&launcher))`, then run a frame if the launcher is closed. Read controls with `ph_input_mask(&input, player)`, ORing in `ph_touch_mask(&touch, &input)` for player 1.
6. **Pausing:** a single-player game can stop in place on `PH_LAUNCH_PAUSE`: run a small loop that feeds events to the launcher and draws it over the last frame until `RESUME`, `RESET`, `END` or `QUIT` comes back. In LAN play the other machine keeps going, so keep running frames while the pause menu is open.
7. **LAN:** on `NETPLAY`, call `ph_net_begin`, read `ph_net_agreed_rules`, and start the game from power on. Feed each frame through `ph_net_frame`. The launcher reports stalls, and turns a lost session into `END`.
8. **Ending:** treat `END` as the one place a game is torn down, whether the player quit, left LAN play, or the other player went away.
9. **ROM:** on `ROM_PICKED`, check the file, `ph_import` it as `rom_import`, search again, report the result, then call `ph_launcher_rom_imported`. On `ROM_RESCAN`, search again if no ROM is loaded.
10. **Settings:** apply the changed setting on `SETTING`, and call `ph_config_save` on `SETTING` and `SAVE_CONFIG`.
11. **Testing:** give the port a `--ui-script` option that calls `ph_script_step` after each presented frame.

## Debug overlay

```c
ph_debug_frame(&debug, work_ms);
if (ph_debug_begin(&debug, renderer)) {
    if (ph_debug_tab(&debug, "Video")) {
        ph_debug_toggle(&debug, "Show sprites", &show_sprites);
        ph_debug_stepper(&debug, "Layer", &layer, 0, 3, 1);
    }
    if (ph_debug_tab(&debug, "Memory")) {
        ph_debug_memory(&debug, ram, sizeof ram, 0x100000, &offset);
    }
    if (ph_debug_tab(&debug, "Net")) {
        ph_debug_network(&debug, &net);
    }
    ph_debug_end(&debug);
}
```

F1 toggles it, as does a four-finger tap. Clicks inside the panel are consumed by `ph_debug_event`.

## Tests and demo

```sh
cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build
./build/ph_demo
```

`tests/test.c` checks hashes, zip and inflate, settings and config file round trips, touch hit testing and action masks, launcher navigation, ROM handling during and between games, UI script parsing and PNG shots, and a real loopback LAN session that runs discovery, connection, agreed rules, 300 lockstep frames, a stall, a forced desync and a refused mismatched game. It also renders every launcher page (in the default theme and in OBG's green theme with a background and logo), the pause menu in desktop and touch sizes, the rebinding prompt, text samples, the touch overlay, the arrange editor and the debug overlay to `tests/out/*.png`. `tests/fixture.py` regenerates the zip and deflate fixtures.

`demo/demo.c` is a small two-player coin chase that uses everything: the launcher, rebinding, touch controls, save states, LAN play and the debug overlay.
